operational-example.copy: Use Tabs to switch between sibling content sections that share one context, such as wallet detail, movement history, settings, or dashboard views.

scenario.title: Wallet detail sections
rationale: Flow defines selected/current as action-primary and keeps Tabs scoped to sibling views in one context.
The reference treatment informs the pill/underline structures, indicator travel, width change, and inertial feel.
Tabs remains visually distinct from Segmented Control through pill or underline navigation treatment and panel association.

rows.label: Motion benchmark
rows.value: Indicator travels and resizes with inertial easing.

rows.label: Boundary
rows.value: Sibling content navigation only; local mode switches use Segmented Control.

items.rule: Owns the accessible grouping and keyboard relationship.
Names one sibling section and exposes selected state.
Shows active selection with Flow action-primary, inertial travel, and width change; this motion is the benchmark for selection components.
Shows compact count while tab label remains the primary name.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, focus, selected, hover, overflow, default
items: Use tablist, tab, and tabpanel semantics.
Expose exactly one selected tab in single-select tabs.
Keep tab labels visible and concise.
Do not use tabs for unrelated destinations or primary navigation.

variants.copy: Tabs supports two approved visual treatments: default for the pill track and underline for flatter navigation surfaces. Both keep the selected indicator travel that defines Tabs momentum.

states.copy: Tabs states communicate active view, hover, focus, overflow, disabled, and default availability. Selected/current uses Flow action-primary while the indicator preserves inertial travel and width change.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant sets the visual treatment; state changes interaction feedback without changing tab semantics.

full-width.copy: Tabs may occupy container width, but each tab keeps label-driven sizing unless product chooses equal-width mobile tabs.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Responsive Tabs preserve section identity: show the default pill treatment with enough room to read labels, then scroll only when the item count needs it.

viewport-organization.copy: Use tabs when content sections are peers. Keep the default pill treatment legible before adding more items.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use short labels and enough width for the active pill.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Allow the tablist to breathe before adding counts or icons.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use more labels only when the container provides enough room.

playground.copy: Use the playground to confirm visual treatment, label length, active state, item count, and density before Tabs enters a template or pattern.

api-foundations.copy: Tabs API exposes label, items, selectedKey, onValueChange, and variant while Design System foundations own active indication, keyboard behavior, indicator momentum, and responsive layout.

props.name: items
props.type: Array<{ key?: string; value?: string; label: string; icon?: string; count?: number; badge?: BadgeProps; disabled?: boolean }>
props.notes: List of sibling sections with optional icon and badge metadata.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Called when local tab selection changes.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Visual treatment for sibling section navigation.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for sibling sections within one object or process.
Keep tab labels short and stable.
Use badges only as secondary counts.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use tabs for global navigation.
Do not hide unrelated destinations inside tabs.
Do not compress labels until they become unreadable.

groups.title: Review
items: Preserve selected/current Flow primary and inertial indicator travel.

mustTest: Indicator travels and resizes with inertial easing
rejectIf: Tabs component demos render through docs-only tabs-demo instead of the package Tabs.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Tabs as sibling-view navigation inside one context: agents can assemble items and active state, while humans confirm information architecture and whether the structure belongs in a pattern.
canDecide: Use Tabs for peer sections inside one object, dashboard, or detail view.
Use the default pill treatment unless product explicitly defines a larger navigation pattern.
Attach Badge only when the count belongs to a tab label.
mustAsk: The sections are not siblings or change global navigation.
The tab count, ordering, or labels are product-critical.
The tabs hide a process that should become a pattern or template.
rejectIf: Tabs are used for unrelated routes.
Keyboard or panel association is missing.
miel.handoff: I am using Tabs for sibling content in one context. I need confirmation on section IA, default selected tab, and whether this should escalate to a pattern.
